article_title: Report on CHIIR 2026 Workshop on Generative AI and Academic Search (GAI&AS)
citation: Yifan Liu, Jaime Arguello, Orland Hoeber, Chang Liu, Soo Young Rieh, Luanne Sinnamon, et al. (2026). Report on CHIIR 2026 Workshop on Generative AI and Academic Search (GAI&AS). ACM SIGIR Forum. https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08936
title: 15-week digital literacy curriculum integrating GenAI tool usage with research ethics and critical thinking
description: A lightning talk by Jiwoo Seo described a "15-week digital literacy curriculum" co-developed during their tenure as an AI Specialist Librarian at Chung-Ang University, "based on a survey of 2,076 students and 101 librarians". The curriculum addressed a critical gap by integrating GenAI tool usage with research ethics and critical thinking skills. It emerged from observing a trust gap in which students often over-trusted GenAI while faculty distrusted it, and it aims to empower users to act as critical reviewers rather than passive consumers.
requirements: sustainable educational frameworks that adapt to rapid AI advancements, since single-session workshops are insufficient
target_learning_goals: GenAI literacy, research ethics, and critical thinking for academic search
examples: the curriculum was co-developed at Chung-Ang University grounded in a survey of 2,076 students and 101 librarians
key_sources: Yifan Liu, Jaime Arguello, Orland Hoeber, Chang Liu, Soo Young Rieh, Luanne Sinnamon, et al. (2026). Report on CHIIR 2026 Workshop on Generative AI and Academic Search (GAI&AS). ACM SIGIR Forum. https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08936

article_title: Application of Make a Match Model to Improve Geography Learning Outcomes
citation: Arisanty, D., Riyah. (2019). Application of make a match model to improve geography learning outcomes. Journal of Technology and Science Education, 9(1), 32-40. https://doi.org/10.3926/jotse.547
title: 15-item multiple-choice geography learning outcomes test with validity, reliability, difficulty and discrimination checks
description: The study's instrument is a multiple-choice test of 15 questions used to measure geography learning outcomes. Before use it was checked for validity, reliability, level of difficulty and differentiating power; Table 1 reports item values (e.g. validity 0.592, reliability 1.041, difficulty 0.304, discrimination 0.435 for item 1) and all items were marked Used.
requirements: Validity, reliability, difficulty and discrimination testing before deployment, as the article describes for its instrument
target_learners: Class X senior high school geography students
examples: Item 9 showed very high validity (0.835), easy difficulty (0.739) and very good discrimination (0.435) and was used in the test.
key_sources: Arisanty, D., Riyah. (2019). Application of make a match model to improve geography learning outcomes. Journal of Technology and Science Education, 9(1), 32-40. https://doi.org/10.3926/jotse.547

article_title: The Effect of Performance Assessment-Driven Instruction on the Attitude and Achievement of Senior High School Students in Mathematics in Cape Coast Metropolis, Ghana
citation: Ato Kwamina Arhin. (2015). The Effect of Performance Assessment-Driven Instruction on the Attitude and Achievement of Senior High School Students in Mathematics in Cape Coast Metropolis, Ghana. Journal of Education and Practice, 6(2). http://www.iiste.org
title: Fifteen-item five-point Likert-type attitude-to-mathematics questionnaire
description: A five-point Likert-type questionnaire of fifteen questions on students' attitude towards mathematics, developed for this study and adapted from a questionnaire developed by Thomas and Emereole (2002) for investigating computer-based instruction in physics in Botswana. Statements cover enjoyment, motivation, understanding with worked examples, creativity, dislike of mathematics, and perceived importance of mathematics. Its reliability estimate was 0.64, and a cut-off point of 50 was used as a measure of positive attitude.
requirements: Administered before and after treatment to detect attitude change
constraints: The article states attitude scales are of limited validity and do not predict behaviour very well
target_learners: senior high school Form 1 science students
examples: 42 experimental-group students responded on both occasions, before and after the treatment
key_sources: Ato Kwamina Arhin. (2015). The Effect of Performance Assessment-Driven Instruction on the Attitude and Achievement of Senior High School Students in Mathematics in Cape Coast Metropolis, Ghana. Journal of Education and Practice, 6(2). https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1083838

article_title: Linking EFL psychological capital and EFL achievement: the chain mediating effect of academic boredom and behavioural engagement.
citation: Wu Yajun, Kang Xia, Li Yiyan. (2025). Linking EFL psychological capital and EFL achievement: the chain mediating effect of academic boredom and behavioural engagement. BMC Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40359-025-03685-x
title: 15-item EFL PsyCap scale with four subscales (optimism, hope, resilience, self-efficacy)
description: A 15-item scale adapted from the School Psychological Capital Scale, comprising four components: optimism (four items), hope (four items), resilience (four items) and self-efficacy (three items). It exhibited good internal consistency in this study: "Cronbach's α = 0.98" overall, with subscales α = 0.78, 0.77, 0.74, 0.76. The article states it can be employed to assess PsyCap profiles among EFL learners within the CHC context and treats PsyCap as a higher-order latent variable in SEM.
requirements: Translation and back-translation to establish equivalence in the target language context
constraints: Validated specifically for Chinese educational / CHC EFL contexts per the article
key_sources: Wu Yajun, Kang Xia, Li Yiyan. (2025). Linking EFL psychological capital and EFL achievement: the chain mediating effect of academic boredom and behavioural engagement. BMC Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40359-025-03685-x

article_title: Comparison of accuracy and consistency of AI Language models when answering standardised dental MCQs.
citation: Alshammari Abdullah F., Madfa Ahmed A., Anazi Bassam Ali, Alenezi Yousef E., Alkurdi Khlood A. (2025). Comparison of accuracy and consistency of AI Language models when answering standardised dental MCQs. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07624-7
title: 150-question standardised dental MCQ benchmark drawn from two NBDE preparation textbooks
description: The study built a text-only benchmark of 150 single-best-answer MCQs randomly selected from two recognised dentistry textbooks (Dental Decks Part II, 2013; First Aid for the NBDE Part II, 2012), covering specialties from operative dentistry to paediatric dentistry. Questions were "independently reviewed and validated by two licensed dental faculty members prior to inclusion", and image-based items were excluded to keep input uniform across models. The same set was administered identically to all five models in both sessions.
requirements: Questions must be text-only, single-best-answer with four options, excluding items requiring visual interpretation
constraints: The article notes the 150-MCQ dataset may not fully capture the breadth of all dental subdisciplines
target_learners: dental students preparing for licensing-style examinations
target_learning_goals: assessment of dental factual and clinical knowledge across major dental specialties
examples: Each of the five AI models was presented with the same 150 MCQs, manually entered in identical format and order without additional prompts or contextual cues.
key_sources: Alshammari Abdullah F., Madfa Ahmed A., Anazi Bassam Ali, Alenezi Yousef E., Alkurdi Khlood A. (2025). Comparison of accuracy and consistency of AI Language models when answering standardised dental MCQs. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07624-7

article_title: Human-Centered Design in Graduate Nursing Education: Outcomes From a Cohort Study.
citation: Holt JM, Talsma A, Lloren JIC, Eljarrah I, Woehrle L, Avdeev I. (2025). Human-Centered Design in Graduate Nursing Education: Outcomes From a Cohort Study. Nurse Educator. https://doi.org/10.1097/NNE.0000000000001778
title: 150-minute in-person Innovation and Human-Centered Design (I&HCD) workshop
description: A 150-minute in-person experiential workshop developed and refined during a pilot phase and facilitated by the author team following "a detailed agenda to ensure intervention fidelity." The team has degrees in "nursing, sociology, peace studies, and engineering" and completed formal and informal training in design thinking and HCD methodologies. Workshop components were developed by applying the 5E Instructional Model (engagement, exploration, explanation, elaboration, evaluation), with experiential exploration before concepts are labeled and defined, including brainstorming, preliminary design solutions, and reflection. Online pre- and posttest surveys and a 4-question reflection survey accompanied the workshop.
requirements: Facilitators with training in design thinking and HCD methodologies and a detailed agenda to ensure intervention fidelity
constraints: The article studied the workshop during graduate school orientation and measured outcomes immediately post-workshop only
target_learners: Master of Nursing, Master of Sustainable Peacebuilding, Doctor of Nursing Practice, and PhD students
target_learning_goals: creative self-efficacy, psychological empowerment, and design thinking traits
examples: Three workshop cohorts (April 2022 n = 32, August 2022 n = 7, August 2023 n = 25) completed the workshop with paired pre/post surveys
key_sources: Holt JM, Talsma A, Lloren JIC, Eljarrah I, Woehrle L, Avdeev I. (2025). Human-Centered Design in Graduate Nursing Education: Outcomes From a Cohort Study. Nurse Educator. https://doi.org/10.1097/NNE.0000000000001778

article_title: Focused educational intervention improves intern knowledge of perioperative patient blood management principles.
citation: Wyssusek K, Taylor K, Concha-Blamey S. (2021). Focused educational intervention improves intern knowledge of perioperative patient blood management principles. BMJ Open Quality. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjoq-2021-001390
title: 15-question perioperative PBM multiple-choice questionnaire developed from NBA and NSQHS guidelines
description: A 15-question multiple-choice questionnaire "formulated by members of the perioperative PBM group at RBWH using information attained from NBA's PBM guidelines and NSQHS Chapter 7: Blood and blood products". It was peer-reviewed by department staff not involved in development to remove ambiguous or misleading questions, then administered pre-intervention and 5 weeks post-intervention. The article notes no validated PBM-specific assessment tool previously existed.
requirements: Reviewed by department staff not involved in development to identify ambiguous or misleading questions and ensure reasonable length
constraints: The article states there is no validated tool to assess the broad spectrum of PBM-specific content and recommends future validation of one unique questionnaire
examples: Distributed face-to-face in paper format before the intervention and again 5 weeks later under facilitator supervision
key_sources: Wyssusek K, Taylor K, Concha-Blamey S. (2021). Focused educational intervention improves intern knowledge of perioperative patient blood management principles. BMJ Open Quality. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjoq-2021-001390
